contentList.content: Battle Affliction

A foe counts as being under a battle affliction while it is <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="STUNNED">stunned</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="FRIGHTENED">frightened</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="CRIPPLED">maimed</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="BLEEDING">bleeding</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="CHEST_TRAUMA">chest wounded</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="DAZED">dazed</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="GAPING_WOUND">deeply wounded</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="HAMSTRING">hamstrung</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="OFF_BALANCED">off balance</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="PRONE">prone</LSTag> or <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="HINDERED">hindered</LSTag>.
High Muster of Netheril

Every boss you fell in open battle while wearing this ring earns you Glory in the High Muster of Netheril. Glory raises your rank, and a rank once earned is never lost.

Every rank makes you more skilled in the art of war. Choose the war doctrines of the Muster, make each rank you earn your own, and become the new Sovereign of Netheril, the one they will tell stories about.

This ring bears no rank above Veteran.

Every rank makes you more skilled in the art of war. Choose the war doctrines of the Muster, make each rank you earn your own, and become the new Sovereign of Netheril, the one they will tell stories about.

This ring bears no rank above Bannerman.

Recruit

Your standing in the High Muster of Netheril: Recruit.

Fell [1] bosses in open battle in all to earn the next rank.

Against a target under a battle affliction you also deal [2] with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks.

They are starting to whisper about you.
Veteran

Your standing in the High Muster of Netheril: Veteran.

Fell [1] bosses in open battle in all to earn the next rank.

Against a target under a battle affliction you also deal [2] with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks.

The Muster opens your first war doctrine to you.
Bannerman

Your standing in the High Muster of Netheril: Bannerman.

Fell [1] bosses in open battle in all to earn the next rank.

Against a target under a battle affliction you also deal [2] with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks.

The Muster opens a doctrine of the second step to you.
Captain

Your standing in the High Muster of Netheril: Captain.

Fell [1] bosses in open battle in all to earn the next rank.

Against a target under a battle affliction you also deal [2] with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks.

You may give orders, one in a battle.
Warlord

Your standing in the High Muster of Netheril: Warlord.

Fell [1] bosses in open battle in all to earn the next rank.

Against a target under a battle affliction you also deal [2] with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks.

The Muster opens a doctrine of the third step to you, and you give orders once a turn.
Sovereign

Your standing in the High Muster of Netheril: Sovereign.

The Muster holds no rank above yours.

Against a target under a battle affliction you also deal [1] with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks.

You give orders without count.
Cormyrean Doctrine I

You skimmed a book of Cormyrean soldiers' jokes, and came to understand the attack a little better.

You now deal an extra [1] (the damage shown follows the weapon in your hand) to targets under a battle affliction with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks, but have [2] less Armour Class.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features.
Cormyrean Doctrine II

You worked your way through the Cormyrean barracks manuals, and came to understand the attack far better than before.

You now deal an extra [1] (the damage shown follows the weapon in your hand) to targets under a battle affliction with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks, but have [2] less Armour Class.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Cormyrean Doctrine III

You went deep into the serious treatises of the Cormyrean elite, and now command the onslaught as no one else does.

You now deal an extra [1] (the damage shown follows the weapon in your hand) to targets under a battle affliction with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks, and lower your Critical Hit threshold with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks by [3], but have [2] less Armour Class.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Baldurian Doctrine I

You listened to enough guardhouse gossip in Rivington to grow a little better at defence.

You now have [1] more Armour Class, but lost [2] Movement Speed.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features.
Baldurian Doctrine II

You leafed through a history of the great Baldurans, and came to see the theory of defence more deeply.

You now have [1] more Armour Class, but lost [2] Movement Speed.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Baldurian Doctrine III

You argued with the head of the Flaming Fist for days and nights, and became a master of defence in depth.

You now have [1] more Armour Class and take [2] less damage from weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks, but lost [3] Movement Speed.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Cormanthan Doctrine I

You found a few elven sketches from Cormanthor about the soldier's daily life, and came to understand movement slightly better.

You now have [1] more Movement Speed.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features.
Cormanthan Doctrine II

You talked a Cormanthan elf into parting with an ancient manuscript on hidden tactics, and came to understand movement better than most.

You now have [1] more Movement Speed, and can Disengage as a Bonus Action.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Cormanthan Doctrine III

You broke open a cache of Cormanthan royal treatises and studied them to the last page, becoming an unmatched master of mobility.

You now have [1] more Movement Speed, can Disengage as a Bonus Action, and regain all your movement after killing a target under a battle affliction.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Impilturan Doctrine I

You took in a couple of rumours about the greatness of Impiltur, and came to know your own strengths a little better.

You now regain [1] point of your main class resource after killing a target under a battle affliction, once in a battle.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features.
Impilturan Doctrine II

You read an old Impilturan bulletin about a paladin order, and came to know more about gathering energy.

You now regain [1] point of your main class resource after killing a target under a battle affliction, twice in a battle.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Impilturan Doctrine III

You found an ancient treatise of the paladins of Impiltur, and became a great scholar of inner strength.

You now regain [1] point of your main class resource after killing a target under a battle affliction, once a turn.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Calishite Doctrine I

You listened to a couple of Calishite tales about bandits, and came to understand the tricks of war a little better.

You now inflict a random battle affliction for [1] turns when you hit a target with a weapon, unarmed or thrown attack, once in a battle.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features.
Calishite Doctrine II

You ordered embroidered Calishite carpets showing the great desert battles, and saw the hidden patterns of war.

You now inflict a random battle affliction for [1] turns when you hit a target with a weapon, unarmed or thrown attack, once in a battle.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Calishite Doctrine III

You found a Calishite merchant and made him share the cunning of the art of war, becoming an unmatched fighter of the desert.

You now inflict a random battle affliction for [1] turns when you hit a target with a weapon, unarmed or thrown attack, once a turn.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Zhentarim Doctrine I

You spent time with a Zhentarim caravan, and came to know supply and logistics slightly better.

You now regain [1] point of each main class resource after every Short Rest, if you killed at least one enemy under a battle affliction since the last one.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features.
Zhentarim Doctrine II

You found a secret Zhentarim treatise on logistics, and multiplied your grasp of that science.

You now regain [1] point of each main class resource and your full Hit Points after every Short Rest, if you killed at least one enemy under a battle affliction since the last one.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Zhentarim Doctrine III

You hired a retired Zhentarim adviser, and bought the most hidden knowledge of logistics.

You now regain [1] point of each main class resource and your full Hit Points after every battle in which you killed at least one enemy under a battle affliction.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Netherese Doctrine I

You began to study the old Netherese runes, understood nothing in them, and still carried away a few lessons in domination.

You now deal an extra [1] (the damage shown follows the weapon in your hand) with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks against enemies below [2]% Hit Points.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features.
Netherese Doctrine II

You commissioned a translation of the Netherese enchantments on your own artefacts, and grew far surer in handling that legacy.

You now deal an extra [1] (the damage shown follows the weapon in your hand) with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks against enemies below [2]% Hit Points, and regain a Bonus Action when you kill an enemy under a battle affliction.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Netherese Doctrine III

You put a request to the High Muster of Netheril, were granted a secret treatise on the art of war, and rose from the reading a great master of battle.

You now deal an extra [1] (the damage shown follows the weapon in your hand) with weapon, unarmed and thrown attacks against enemies below [2]% Hit Points, and regain an Action when you kill an enemy under a battle affliction.

Once chosen, the doctrine appears among your passive features. A doctrine of the same culture is replaced by this one.
Strategist
Allies within [1] gain +[2] to Attack Rolls and +[3] to their Spell Save DC.
You gain +[1] to Attack Rolls and +[2] to your Spell Save DC.
Champion

Killing a creature restores your Action, once a turn.

Reduces your Critical Hit threshold against a target under a battle affliction by [1].
Orders

Give an order to your party, raising its fighting strength for a time.

A Captain gives one order in a battle, a Warlord one a turn, a Sovereign is held to no count.
Hold the Line!
For [3] turns, allies within [1] gain [2] and cannot be knocked prone.
Advance!
For [5] turns, allies within [1] gain +[2] Movement Speed and +[3] to Attack Rolls, and their first attack each turn pushes the target [4] away.
Re-Form!
Allies within [1] shed Frightened, Hamstrung, Off Balance and fleeing, once.
Choose a Doctrine
Choose the war doctrine you will follow. At every rank you may take a further doctrine with stronger benefits.
The Last Question
The Muster asks what kind of soldier you turned out to be. The choice cannot be undone.
